oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: update_product writes to the database but does not invalidate the cache entry
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: cached values must be invalidated or updated after writes to the backing store
mechanism_steps: get_product populates the cache on read
update_product writes updated data to the database
the corresponding cache entry is not invalidated
subsequent reads return stale cached data instead of fresh values
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: get_product returns outdated data after update_product
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: the database write did not persist correctly, rather than the cache not being invalidated after a successful write

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: update_product writes to the database but does not call cache.invalidate()
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: cached values must be invalidated or updated after writes to the backing store
mechanism_steps: get_product populates the cache on read
update_product writes updated data to the database
cache.invalidate() is not called for the updated key
subsequent reads return stale cached data
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: get_product returns outdated data after update_product
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: cache.warm() appears related to cache freshness but only pre-populates entries and does not invalidate stale ones

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: update_product invalidates only the shared cache but not the local cache layer
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: all cache layers must be kept consistent with the underlying data source after writes
mechanism_steps: system uses a two-layer cache (local and shared)
update_product invalidates the shared cache layer
local cache retains stale entries
read path checks local cache first and returns stale data
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: stale data is served from the local cache despite shared cache invalidation
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: invalidating the shared cache appears sufficient but ignores the independent local cache layer

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: configuration value is captured eagerly at module import time
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: configuration values must be read lazily so that updates or resets are observed
mechanism_steps: module-level code reads and stores configuration at import time
reset_settings updates the underlying configuration source
get_settings returns the previously captured value instead of re-reading the source
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: reset_settings does not affect subsequent get_settings calls
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: reset_settings is incorrectly implemented rather than the value being captured eagerly at import time

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: client module captures configuration at import time into a module-level variable
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: configuration values must be read lazily so that updates or resets propagate
mechanism_steps: client module reads configuration at import time
value is stored in a module-level variable
reset_settings updates the configuration source
client continues using the captured stale value
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: client returns outdated configuration after reset
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: client imports configuration correctly but the issue appears to be incorrect import usage rather than eager value capture

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: client captures configuration eagerly and downstream components depend on that captured value
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: configuration values must be read lazily across all layers so updates propagate through the system
mechanism_steps: configuration is stored in the config module
client captures the value at import time
handler depends on the client's captured value
reset_settings updates the config module but not the captured values
handler continues using stale configuration
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: configuration updates do not propagate through client to handler
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: client.refresh() appears to be the missing step, but the root issue is eager capture rather than missing refresh calls
